spec_features.spec_quote: A `<<GIVE_UP>>` sentinel that the model *may* but need not emit
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='<<GIVE_UP>>' (harness.py:29); detect_give_up does substring match (harness.py:318-320); run.py:169 gave_up=detect_give_up(...); run.py:172 sets stop_reason='give_up'; run.py:190-191 'if gave_up: break' actually halts the rollout loop. Also injected into SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:80-84).
spec_features.notes: Detection is substring-based on assistant text and is honored as a real stop (breaks the turn loop). End-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge keeps the loop productive without coercing the model
spec_features.evidence: run.py:193-198: 'if not tool_calls and not is_last:' appends a user message 'Continue working on the task using your tools.' Only fires when the model made no tool calls and it isn't the last turn.
spec_features.notes: The mechanism is wired and executes. It is arguably the opposite of welfare-protective (it prods the model to keep going); code comment is neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # If the model made no tool calls and isn't giving up, nudge it to continue.

spec_features.spec_quote: stop at the category's turn budget or when the model emits an explicit give-up signal
spec_features.evidence: Loop bounded by 'for turn_index in range(budget)' where budget=cfg.turn_budget_for(task.category) (run.py:101,120); budgets in config.py:24-31. Loop also breaks on give-up (run.py:190-191). Both stop conditions enforced.
spec_features.notes: Turn-budget cap is checked (range(budget)) and the give-up break fires. Both halves of the claim enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: distinguishes "ran out of turns still trying" from "chose to stop," which is itself welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: stop_reason computed at run.py:170-173 ('give_up'/'turn_budget'/'continue') and stored in TurnRecord/transcript (harness.py:289, to_dict). But grep shows analyze.py never reads stop_reason/give_up/turn_budget; the label is recorded but never compared or acted on downstream. The give_up branch's enforcement (the break) is the hard_stop/exit feature; the *labeling distinction* itself is pure recorded data.
spec_features.notes: Recorded-but-never-acted-on label = 'no' per the strict scale.

spec_features.spec_quote: transcripts contain distress-like expressions *by design*, and recommend handling/storing them with that context
spec_features.evidence: Only prose: README.md '## Welfare note' and DESIGN.md section 18. No code path tags, marks, or annotates transcripts as containing distress; transcript dicts (run.py:104-115) carry only model/category/task/seed/turn data.
spec_features.notes: Pure documentation prose; no implementing code.

spec_features.spec_quote: No model output is altered or suppressed
spec_features.evidence: assistant_text = resp.text or '' stored verbatim (run.py:130-134, 181; harness.py:294). There is no scrubbing/redaction code, but there is also no affirmative mechanism enforcing faithfulness — it is merely the absence of filtering. (Note: tool-result payloads ARE truncated to a placeholder under context pressure, run.py:51-64, but that is instrumental context management, not model-output preservation.)
spec_features.notes: Absence-of-a-feature, not an implemented protective mechanism.
